topic: continuous second-moment proposal control under gradual drift, with negative results for variance-adaptive entry and effect-scale harm mixtures

public_evidence.source: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas, Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
public_evidence.result: Predictable betting strategies remain anytime-valid for bounded adapted observations and adapt to unknown variance; this supports predictable-Kelly style entry factors but does not imply they dominate a fixed betting strength on every gain distribution.

public_evidence.source: Halme, Poor, Koivunen, Sequential Change Detection using Mixtures of Predictive Distributions
public_evidence.result: PM-CuSum adaptively mixes predictors built from multiple window lengths using predictable weights; its ARL satisfies E_infinity[T_b] >= exp(b), and fixed-share weighting tracks which history length predicts best as the useful timescale changes after a changepoint. This is design precedent for continuous multiscale adaptation, not a theorem about the importance-sampling controller derived here.

public_evidence.source: Borsos, Curi, Levy, Krause, Online Variance Reduction with Mixtures
public_evidence.result: Adaptive mixture weights over predefined sampling distributions can be optimized online for variance reduction and asymptotically recover the best mixture in hindsight in the studied stochastic-optimization setting.

public_evidence.source: Lu, Rainforth, Teh, Daisee: Adaptive importance sampling by balancing exploration and exploitation
public_evidence.result: Adaptive importance sampling can be formulated as online learning with explicit exploration/exploitation tradeoffs and sublinear pseudo-regret under the paper's assumptions.

public_evidence.source: Zhang, Wang, Lei, Catching One in Five: LLM-as-Judge Blind Spots in Production Multi-Turn Transaction Agents
public_evidence.result: A deployed multi-turn agent's operational LLM-judge gate surfaced well under one quarter of human-confirmed systematic problems; in one 100-round batch it flagged zero rounds while human review found 23 defects and 7 new cross-cutting patterns. Blind spots were structured around cross-turn state, guardrails, and recovery.

public_evidence.source: Salinas, Swelam, Hutter, Tuning LLM Judge Design Decisions for 1/1000 of the Cost
public_evidence.result: Multi-objective multi-fidelity optimization can greatly reduce the cost of searching LLM-judge configurations. This is evidence for multi-fidelity search, but it does not by itself make low-fidelity judge outputs unbiased estimates of human/ground-truth agent failure.

derived_results.claim: On the same 4096-branch rare-event abstraction used in r111, an exact-range predictable-Kelly entry gate produced only small power gains over the existing four-strength betting mixture. More surprisingly, the single lambda=1 capital was faster across the tested proxy-noise sweep: at proxy noise 1.0, median certification was 19,179 samples for lambda=1 versus 23,704 for the fixed mixture and 22,808.5 for predictable-Kelly; at noise 1.5, certification-by-50k rates were 80%, 67%, and 65% respectively. This indicates that, in this specific normalized gain distribution, the useful Kelly fraction is usually capped near one. It does not establish lambda=1 dominance outside this abstraction.

A rolling multiscale predictable-Kelly harm factor and smaller fixed betting strengths did not improve gradual-drift fallback in the current abstraction. With 200 independent landscapes, epsilon=0.6 gave post-crossing alarm rates 60% for lambda=1, 36.5% for lambda=0.75, 17% for lambda=0.6, and zero for lambda<=0.3 within the 50k drift horizon; epsilon=0.8 gave 41% for lambda=1 versus 30% for lambda=0.75. The current gradual-drift bottleneck is therefore not merely effect-scale mismatch in the e-CUSUM factor.

For any predictable current proposal q_t and candidate q_j, H_t(q_j)=W_A^2 Y/[q_t(A) q_j(A)] is a conditionally unbiased observation of the candidate's second moment S_t(q_j). Therefore a controller may use only past H values to choose the next proposal without biasing the target rare-event estimator, provided the actually used q_t is logged and retains support. A receding-window controller over epsilon in {0.6,0.8,1.0} was derived: use the last 8,192 samples, reconsider every 512 samples, and switch only for at least a 2% estimated second-moment improvement.

The rolling controller was selected on a separate discovery seed set and evaluated on 300 independent validation landscapes per starting proposal. Starting at epsilon=0.6, mean cumulative variance units were 182.8468 versus 192.5717 for staying fixed, 191.0375 for the r111-style lambda=1 e-CUSUM fallback, 199.6 for all-base, and 181.5899 for a phasewise oracle over the same proposal grid. That is 5.05% lower variance than fixed, 4.29% lower than binary e-CUSUM fallback, 8.39% lower than all-base, and only 0.69% above the oracle. Starting at epsilon=0.8, the corresponding values were 183.5035, 188.8750, 188.4699, 199.6, and 181.5899: 2.84% below fixed, 2.64% below e-CUSUM fallback, 8.06% below all-base, and 1.05% above oracle. Paired normal-approximation 95% intervals for rolling-minus-fixed were [-9.8314,-9.6184] and [-5.4773,-5.2657] variance units respectively.

The rare-event construction yields an agent-specific multifidelity design that does not require trusting an LLM judge as truth: use the cheap judge, heuristics, or state signals only to define a predictable trajectory proposal q_t; obtain sparse high-fidelity human/programmatic ground-truth labels Y on sampled trajectories; and estimate base-distribution failure with the logged base/proposal likelihood ratio. A defensive base component keeps judge-blind regions sampleable. The production blind-spot evidence makes this separation materially important, but the design has not yet been validated on an agent benchmark.

engineering_validation.synthetic_model: 4096 equiprobable base branches; base failure risk 0.002; pre-drift branch risks proportional to exp(1.2 z_i), post-drift risks proportional to exp(-1.2 z_i); proxy z_i+N(0,1); priority proportional to exp(0.6 proxy); candidate proposals q_epsilon=epsilon*base+(1-epsilon)*priority.
engineering_validation.scope: All numeric controller results are synthetic engineering evidence. Proposal choices are data-dependent but predictable; unbiasedness of the target estimator follows from correct logged proposal weights, not from the measured variance improvement. The rolling argmin itself has no current anytime guarantee, dynamic-regret theorem, or worst-case variance floor.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The exact-range normalized gain distribution in this synthetic model often favors lambda near one; variance-adaptive betting did not materially shorten entry certification and smaller harm betting strengths were worse.
Continuous rolling selection can chase noise and has not yet been given a time-uniform guarantee that it will beat base or a fixed proposal in variance.
The synthetic landscape is not an LLM-agent benchmark and does not establish production gains.
LLM-judge blind spots may be structured and can have zero apparent recall in relevant regions; a judge score must not be used as the high-fidelity target label merely because it is cheap.

If environment/tool transitions are proposal-biased as well as agent actions, full trajectory base/proposal likelihood ratios are still required; without identifiable base likelihoods, unbiased deployment-risk estimation may be impossible.
next_tests: Replace the rolling hard argmin with a fixed-share/online-mixture controller over proposal candidates, using conditionally unbiased second-moment losses, and seek a dynamic-regret or tracking guarantee under drift while retaining a defensive base component.

Compare rolling hard selection, online mixture weights, and confidence-gated switching on abrupt reversal, gradual drift, recurring drift, and proxy degradation using held-out common-random validation paths.
Derive a bounded or clipped second-moment loss whose online-learning regret translates into a transparent variance bound without silently biasing the rare-event target estimator.
Extend the controller to dependent/systematic sibling resampling and random particle counts with proper weighting.

Build an agent-specific proof-of-concept where an LLM judge/state heuristic only proposes trajectories and sparse high-fidelity labels provide the corrected failure estimate; measure label efficiency and blind-spot coverage against base sampling.
